rounds.text: Bhartiya International Ltd is exhibiting explosive top-line acceleration, with compounded sales growth reaching 20% over 5 years [E15], 19% over 3 years [E16], and 34% over the trailing twelve months [E17], backed by a rules-based screen scoring 81 out of 100 driven by a 33% YoY sales surge [E66, E67] and a 200% YoY net profit jump [E68]. Furthermore, insiders and management are heavily aligned with shareholders, as demonstrated by promoters increasing their stake to 61.17% in Jun 2026 from 57.35% in Sep 2023 [E42], while capital expenditure is aggressively ramping up with a 300% surge in capital work-in-progress to Rs 12 Cr to fuel future capacity [E41]. Operating cash flows are also robustly backing reported earnings with a 1.46x cash conversion ratio as of Mar 2026 [E34], and the business is benefiting from a supportive macro setup in the Consumer Durables sector tailwind [E72]. Conceded: [E13] and [E28] regarding low historical return on equity figures and [E38] concerning elevated leverage risk.

Bhartiya International Ltd trades at an inflated P/E ratio of 51.4x and a P/B of 2.72x, significantly outpacing sector benchmarks of 25.66x and 1.93x respectively [E1, E2, E6, E7]. This aggressive valuation sits on top of weak fundamental returns, highlighted by a meager 2.9% ROE and a 10-year median ROE of just 4% [E13, E26]. Furthermore, long-term wealth creation has stalled, demonstrated by a -7% compounded profit growth over 10 years and a 3-year profit contraction of -40% [E18, E20]. Balance sheet and cash generation risks compound these concerns, with borrowings rising to Rs 542 Cr, a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.11x indicating debt exceeds net worth, and free cash flow stalling at Rs 0 Cr in March 2026 [E36, E38, E40]. Valuation models confirm this disconnect, as a discounted cash flow analysis places intrinsic value at Rs 796 per share against a market price of Rs 988, resulting in a negative margin of safety of -24.2% [E46, E47]. Conceded: compounded sales growth reached 34% over the trailing twelve months and profit growth is up 33% over 5 years [E17, E19].

Conceded: the P/E ratio stands at 51.4x and P/B is 2.72x [E1, E2], alongside a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 796 per share versus the market price of Rs 988 [E46]. However, focusing solely on static multiples ignores the explosive acceleration in top-line demand, where compounded sales growth reached 34% over the trailing twelve months and 20% over 5 years [E15, E17], significantly outperforming the sector median sales growth of 17.9% [E76]. Conceded: the 10-year compounded profit growth is -7% and 3-year profit growth is -40% [E18, E20]; nevertheless, medium-term and recent metrics show a powerful turnaround with 5-year compounded profit growth at 33% [E19] and quarterly results showing a net profit surge of 200% year-on-year alongside expectations of a good upcoming quarter [E60, E68]. Conceded: long-term ROE has been depressed [E26] and borrowings reached Rs 542 Cr [E40]; however, operating cash flow for March 2026 was fully backed by profits with a cash conversion ratio of 1.46x [E34], and promoter confidence is rising as they increased their stake to 61.17% in June 2026 from 57.35% in September 2023 [E42]. Furthermore, capital expenditure is actively ramping up with capital work-in-progress up 300% to Rs 12 Cr [E41], and technical momentum remains robust with the stock trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages alongside a maximum relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E51, E52].

Conceded: 5-year compounded profit growth is 33% and quarterly profit surged 200% year-on-year [E19, E68]. However, this recent bounce obscures a severe multi-year earnings contraction, evidenced by 10-year compounded profit growth at -7%, 3-year profit growth at -40%, and TTM profit growth slipping -4% [E18, E20, E21]. Conceded: sales grew 34% over the trailing twelve months and 20% over 5 years [E15, E17]. Nonetheless, this top-line expansion fails to generate shareholder returns, as demonstrated by a depressed median ROE of just 2% over the last 3 years and 3% over the last year, alongside a low 3-year average ROE of 2.30% [E28, E29, E64]. Conceded: cash conversion reached 1.46x for March 2026 [E34]. Despite this, absolute free cash flow remained completely flat at Rs 0 Cr, and borrowings expanded to Rs 542 Cr against a low interest coverage ratio, leaving debt exceeding net worth at 1.11x leverage [E36, E38, E40, E63]. Conceded: promoters increased their stake to 61.17% [E42]. Even so, institutional money flow shows negative movement with foreign institutions reducing holdings to 7.43%, while the stock trades at an inflated P/E of 51.4x and a P/B of 2.72x that severely outpaces sector benchmarks [E1, E2, E6, E7, E43, E45]. Conceded: the relative-strength rating sits at 100 with technicals above moving averages [E51, E52]. Yet, expectations have run excessively ahead of delivery with price growth exceeding profit growth by 24%, leaving a negative margin of safety of -24.2% against a discounted cash flow value of Rs 796 [E46, E47, E58].
